key_concepts: Salt is a polar solute that dissolves in polar water, not oil.
"Like dissolves like": polar solvents dissolve polar solutes and nonpolar solvents dissolv
Smaller solute particle size increases surface area and speeds dissolution.
Higher solvent temperature generally increases solubility of solid solutes.
Solubility of gases in liquids decreases as temperature increases.
Decreasing pressure when opening soda lets dissolved gas escape.
Pressure strongly affects gas solubility but has little effect on solid solubility.
Stirring or agitation increases dissolution rate by maintaining solute-solvent contact.
Carbonated drinks are made by forcing carbon dioxide into soda at high pressure.
Solubility is the maximum amount of solute that dissolves in a given solvent at specific t
Heating a saturated solution can make it unsaturated by dissolving more solute.
Boiled water tastes bland because dissolved oxygen and carbon dioxide escape.
